Enum Class GamepadLayout

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<GamepadLayout>
frc.spectrumLib.gamepads.GamepadLayout
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<GamepadLayout>, Constable
public enum GamepadLayout extends Enum<GamepadLayout>
Where an Xbox controller's buttons and axes arrive, which depends on the Driver Station that sends them, not on the robot controller.

The SystemCore HAL copies the joystick arrays it gets from MrcCommDaemon without remapping them (allwpilib v2027.0.0-alpha-6 hal/src/main/native/systemcore/FIRSTDriverStation.cpp), and WPILib ships separate NiDs* controller classes because "the old DS doesn't have the same mappings as a new DS" (allwpilib PR #8376). So:

  • NI_DS: the 2026 NI FRC Driver Station, the one the 2026 FMS supports. The legacy XInput order: A B X Y LB RB Back Start LS RS = buttons 0-9; axes LX LY LT RT RX RY = 0-5; the D-pad is POV 0. The same as WPILib alpha-6's NiDsXboxController. The sim GUI's "Map gamepad" also produces this order for an Xbox controller on Windows.
  • WPILIB_DS: the 2027 WPILib Driver Station (SDL gamepad order). Buttons south east west north back guide start LS RS LB RB = 0-10, the D-pad as buttons 11-14; axes LX LY RX RY LT RT = 0-5. Taken from WPILib's Gamepad.

    • detect

      public static Optional<GamepadLayout> detect(GenericHID hid)
      Guesses which Driver Station layout a connected controller's data is in, from what the DS says the controller has (logged by AdvantageKit, so this replays). Empty when it can't tell.

      This is inferred, not documented: a POV means NI_DS (whatever the button count); button 14 with no POV means WPILIB_DS, whose D-pad is buttons 11-14. Anything else is unknown. Check it with the bench test in the README before trusting AUTO.

      Parameters:
      hid - the controller
      Returns:
      the layout its data looks like, if it is recognisable
